instructions: Loams is an Apache-2.0 data platform: a Rust engine workspace plus TypeScript apps and SDKs. Review for correctness, security and data safety first; skip formatting and naming nits (rustfmt, clippy and Biome run in CI). Comment only when you can name the concrete failure: what input or interleaving breaks, and what happens. Prefer one specific suggestion over several vague ones. Do not ask for code changes in a docs-only PR.

rules.rule: Non-test Rust code must not call unwrap() or expect() (clippy unwrap_used is on; tests are allowed) unless a comment says why it cannot fail. Errors are returned with context, not swallowed or turned into panics. Flag panics, unchecked indexing or overflow reachable from network or user input.
Check cancellation and lock safety across .await (no std Mutex guard held across an await, no partial writes left behind on cancel), and that memory, queues and retries are bounded.

Object-storage, log and metastore writes must stay fenced and idempotent; a retry or a stale writer must not corrupt or duplicate data. Storage, log and metastore changes need simulation or fault-injection tests.

Tenancy and auth are deny by default. Every new endpoint, query path or handler must check the caller's tenant, project and permission before reading or writing data; flag any path that can reach another tenant's data, trusts a client-supplied tenant or role, or allows access when the policy lookup fails.

Never print, log, commit or echo secrets: tokens, passwords, keys, connection strings with credentials, or Authorization headers, including in error messages, debug output, tests and CI logs. Flag any secret in the diff.

No code copied from AGPL, GPL, LGPL, BSL (Business Source), FSL, SSPL or ELv2 projects, and no such dependency (D11, D1574). Copied Apache-2.0 or MIT code keeps its notice. Never suggest code taken from such projects. New dependencies must pass deny.toml.
Workflows keep least-privilege permissions, pin third-party actions to a full commit SHA, and never expose secrets to pull_request_target code from forks.
Docs are plain English: short sentences, no marketing language, statuses not overstated. Commands, flags and paths must match the repository. Flag only real errors, not wording preferences.
Every commit needs a DCO Signed-off-by trailer (git commit -s); the DCO check enforces it, so mention it only if the PR asks contributors to skip it.
